title: Offload aggregation hotspots to async aggregator service
creator: Lena Zhang
description: Triage and remove synchronous aggregation work from hot GraphQL/REST handlers in the Console backend. The current monolithic request path performs multi-source aggregation (usage, cost, model stats, traces) and heavy cache logic inline which increases tail latency and amplifies downstream load. This ticket scopes an incremental refactor: 1) introduce an async aggregator service (internal RPC + persistent cache), 2) extract non-critical enrichment steps from request path, 3) add read-through caching and TTLs tuned per artifact, and 4) create a canary rollout with latency/cost/accuracy SLO gating.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for /console/route X reduced by >= 18% in prod canary
end-to-end error rate for aggregated endpoints remains <= previous baseline
aggregated data freshness SLA: critical fields <= 5s, non-critical <= 60s
no increase in CPU utilization > 10% on console-backend primary fleet after rollout
playbook for rollback and postmortem template added to Confluence
implementation_steps: Benchmark current hotpaths and capture flamegraphs (baseline ticket ENG-27901-BENCH)
Create new internal service: console-aggregator (RPC over internal gRPC, auth via mTLS)
Move non-blocking enrichments (cost breakdown, model-profile hints, analytics tags) to aggregator with read-through cache
Implement KV cache with per-key TTLs and cache invalidation hooks from mutation endpoints
Add feature flag and header-based canary routing; implement 10/50/100% rollout stages
Run integration tests and synthetic load with canary; monitor latency, token-cost, and error budgets
Roll forward to full traffic with gradual scaling and update runbook
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Stale data for some UI tiles -> Mitigation: tiered TTLs and immediate invalidation for mutations
Risk: Increased operational surface -> Mitigation: small stateless aggregator replicas, autoscaling, and alerting
Risk: RPC/serialization overhead adds latency -> Mitigation: protobuf + gzip + connection pooling and benchmark micro-optimizations
Risk: Cache stampede on cold keys -> Mitigation: jittered refreshing, background pre-warming for known hot keys
performance_targets: P50: no change or slight improvement
Token-serving cost per 1k requests: <= 5% delta from baseline

2025-01-21 - Priya Singh (PM): OK to prioritize non-blocking fields first. Customer-facing panels that require strong freshness: make those synchronous until we add invalidation hooks.
2025-01-28 - Asha Patel (SRE): Added observability expectations: request tracing through aggregator, cache hit/miss metrics, and a synthetic transaction to alert on freshness SLA violations.

2025-02-05 - Miguel Torres: Prototype aggregator service implemented (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4287). Early bench shows 15% P95 improvement on dev workloads when enrichment is removed from primary path.
2025-02-12 - Connor O'Neill (Eng reviewer): Reviewed PR; requested changes to error handling and idempotency of background refresh jobs. Also asked to add feature flagging for canary.
2025-02-20 - Miguel Torres: Canary started at 10% on staging cluster. Metrics: P95 down 19%, cache hit 78%, background refresh queue stable. Filed follow-ups for cache TTL tuning (ENG-27901-TTL).
2025-02-24 - Lena Zhang: Security review passed (scope limited to internal RPC, no external surface). Roadmap: expand canary to 50% next week, monitor CPU and egress costs closely.
notes: We intentionally keep the aggregator small and horizontally scalable to limit blast radius.
If we discover regressions in critical fields, we will revert and pursue finer-grained memoization in resolver code instead.
Follow-on work includes: cache TTL tuning (ENG-27901-TTL), eviction instrumentation, and a dashboard to show field-level freshness per tenant.
